;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Macuto Bay raid]], [[United States–Venezuela relations]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] denies any involvement by the U.S. government in Silvercorp USA's armed incursion into [[Venezuela]] on May 3, which left eight people dead and several others captured, including two U.S. citizens. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-venezuela-security-trump/trump-says-us-government-has-nothing-to-do-with-venezuela-situation-idUSKBN22H1XL (Reuters)]
*[[Western Iran clashes (2016–present)]]
**Gunmen kill three [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] (IRGC) members near the [[Kurds in Iran|Kurdish]]-majority city of [[Divandarreh]], in the [[Kurdistan Province]], while "several counterrevolutionaries" are reportedly killed in the fighting, according to [[Iran]]ian media. [https://www.rferl.org/a/three-revolutionary-guards-members-reported-killed-in-western-iran/30594623.html (RFERL)]

;Disasters and accidents
*At least two miners are killed in a [[mine collapse]] in [[Grand Cape Mount County]], [[Liberia]]. The mayor of the county's administrative centre says scores of others are unaccounted for and feared dead. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-liberia-mine-collapse/liberia-ministry-says-two-killed-in-mine-collapse-local-mayor-fears-scores-more-dead-idUSKBN22H1KA (Reuters)]
*A massive fire breaks out at the 48-storey residential skyscraper Abbco Tower in [[Al Nahda]], [[Sharjah]], [[United Arab Emirates|UAE]]. At least 12 people are injured. [https://gulfnews.com/uae/video-my-thoughts-were-on-trying-to-get-my-wife-and-children-out-of-the-apartment-a-tenant-after-massive-fire-erupts-in-sharjah-tower-1.1588700592377 (''Gulf News'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Yemen]]
***The [[Houthis]]-controlled area of [[Yemen]] reports its first case of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] and first death; that of a [[Somalis|Somali]] man who had liver and kidney conditions. The [[government of Yemen|government]] in the south reports nine new infections. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-yemen/yemens-houthis-report-first-coronavirus-case-a-death-in-sanaa-hotel-idUSKBN22H1HL?il=0 (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***[[Brazil]]'s [[Ministry of Health (Brazil)|Ministry of Health]] reports 6,935 new cases of COVID-19 and 600 more deaths, the highest daily death toll in the country to date, bringing the country's death toll to 7,921 and 114,715 total cases. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-brazil/brazil-registers-6935-new-cases-of-coronavirus-600-deaths-on-tuesday-idUSKBN22H33I (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
***The [[Department of Health and Social Care]] reports that the death toll from COVID-19 in the [[United Kingdom]] stands at 29,427, which is now the highest in [[Europe]], after surpassing [[Italy]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-52549860 (BBC News)]

;Law and crime
*The [[Philippines]]' [[National Telecommunications Commission (Philippines)|National Telecommunications Commission]] issues a [[ABS-CBN franchise renewal controversy|cease and desist]] order to the broadcasting operations of [[ABS-CBN Corporation|ABS-CBN]], the country's largest media network, as [[Congress of the Philippines|Congress]] fails to renew its franchise granted in 1995. The network signed off at 7:52 PM, [[Philippine Standard Time]]. The last time the network was shut down was upon the [[Proclamation No. 1081|declaration of martial law]] by the Philippine dictator [[Ferdinand Marcos]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/05/philippines-largest-tv-network-abs-cbn-ordered-shut-200505084440098.html (Al Jazeera)] [https://news.abs-cbn.com/news/05/05/20/ntc-defied-congress-by-issuing-halt-order-vs-abs-cbn-lawmaker-says (ABS-CBN News)] [https://www.rappler.com/nation/259990-abs-cbn-goes-off-air-ntc-order-may-5-2020 (''Rappler'')]
